Alex K.: Dropping the nsys capture from a failed run — seeing a sharp queue-time hump around step 45 for long prompts (~1500 tokens). attaching timeline in thread and short summary below. :eyes:
Maria G.: acked. did you also capture perfetto traces or just nsys?
Alex K.: nsys + a lightweight perfetto on the host. nsys shows a 190ms queue window before the first flash_attn kernel, compute time itself is ~70ms.
Cheng L.: ping: which kernel version got picked? cutlass matmul or triton/flash path? kernel selection logs?
Alex K.: runtime chose flash_attn_v2 for the attention op, cutlass for GEMM. kernel-selection log: `kernel_picker: model=redwood-7b, seq=1536 -> attention=flash_attn_v2, matmul=cutlass_f32x8`
Sam R.: thanks. KV cache hit rate during that run? if prefix cache misses spike we might be doing extra memcpy/lookup which pushes queue time up.
Alex K.: kvcache hit rate printed ~92% but there is a correlated sweep event at step 44 where a background compact triggered (we saw a host->device memcpy burst). linked screenshot of timeline at 00:00:44.
Priya S.: ok that explains part. background GC/compaction during batching window is bad. can you repro with `--kvcache-compact=false`?
Alex K.: reproed with compact disabled: queue hump disappears, tail latency stable. interestingly compute time rose slightly (+5ms) due to larger memory footprint but overall latency wins.
Cheng L.: nice. also check batching heuristics: if continuous_batch.window_ms is 20 vs 50 we might be accumulating more requests that trigger larger kernel launches leading to preemption. what was batch_window?
Alex K.: batch_window_ms=30 in the run. i tried 15 and 60 locally; 15 reduced median but increased variance, 60 increased queue time but improved throughput.
Sam R.: can you paste the nsys kernel timeline snippet? the shape matters (many small kernels back-to-back vs single fat kernel).
Alex K.: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# nsys timeline excerpt
T=44.123s: memcpy H->D 45ms
T=44.170s: flash_attn_v2 kernel 72ms
T=44.254s: cutlass_sgemm 9ms
T=44.265s: kernel_launch_kicker 180ms (queue)
```
Maria G.: that `kernel_launch_kicker` looks like our queue stall where the GPU is waiting on kernel args/stream submission. maybe host-side serialization (mutex) or driver queue saturation.
Priya S.: perf-bot ran microtrace earlier — it flagged a host lock around `BatchQueue::pop()` at ~150us spikes. not 180ms though.
perf-bot: Automated note: recent builds with cuda 12.2 + driver 535.86 have increased enqueue latency in some cases. See internal ticket INF-472.
Cheng L.: combine signals: host GC memcpy + queue_submit path + batchwindow choice -> creates a pathological tail for long prompts. mitigation options: 1) defer compact to maintenance thread with backoff, 2) increase continuous_batch.window_ms to allow coalescing, 3) prefetch KV pages earlier to avoid memcpy during critical path, 4) move kernel launches to a dedicated submission thread to avoid locks.
Sam R.: short experiment plan: (a) disable compact (done), (b) enable submission thread + measure nsys, (c) run with batch_window 60 and 120 to find sweetspot. can you run (b) and upload results?
Alex K.: running (b) now, will post nsys link when done. initial quick run shows queue hump reduced to ~25ms. posting full trace in ~10m. :thumbsup:
Maria G.: nice repro and clear signal. file bug and mark for postmortem if (b) is stable. add perf regression label and link traces.
Alex K.: filing INF-501 with traces + nsys/perfetto links. thanks all.
Maria G.: one more: record model config + kernel-picker debug (`--kernel-debug`) in the ticket so we can replay deterministic picks.
Alex K.: done in the ticket.
